title: A separated etale algebraic space over a scheme is a scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $E$ be an algebraic space over $X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $q:E\to X$ be a morphism. Assume that $q$ is etale in the chartwise sense: for every representable etale morphism $V\to E$ with $V$ a scheme, the composite $V\to X$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume also that its diagonal $E\to E\times_XE$ is a closed immersion, meaning that every scheme base change is a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $E$ is represented by a scheme $Z$ over $X$, and $Z\to X$ is etale. No quasi-compactness assumption is made on $E$ or $q$.

source.place: Tag 03XU (lemma-etale-locally-quasi-finite) and Tag 03XX (proposition-locally-quasi-finite-separated-over-scheme), in Section Tag 0417 (section-schemehood).

proof.text: The chartwise etale hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis of [lem-a1-etale-space-locally-quasi-finite]. Therefore q is locally quasi-finite in the chartwise sense: for every representable etale scheme chart V→E, the composite V→X is locally quasi-finite.

The assumed scheme-base-change condition on the diagonal is precisely separatedness of q: by [def-weil-proper-morphism], a morphism is separated when its diagonal is a closed immersion, and the algebraic-space meaning of closed immersion is the testwise meaning stated in the item.

source.place: Separated morphisms and their diagonal; the algebraic-space testwise convention is the item definition.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-separated-locally-qf-space-representable] with the base scheme S=X, target scheme T=X, algebraic space E, and f=q. It supplies a scheme Z over X and an isomorphism h_Z≅E over X.

Let $\varphi:h_Z\to E$ be the isomorphism over $X$ from step 3. It is a representable etale map from a scheme in the sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space]: for a scheme $T$ and a map $h_T\to E$, the fibre product $h_Z\times_E h_T$ is the base change of the isomorphism $\varphi$, so the projection $h_Z\times_Eh_T\to h_T$ is an isomorphism; the fibre product is thus represented by $T$ and the scheme projection is an isomorphism of schemes, in particular an open immersion, hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1). So $V=Z$ with $V\to E$ equal to $\varphi$ is one of the representable etale scheme charts in the item's chartwise hypothesis, and that hypothesis makes the composite $q\circ\varphi:Z\to X$ an etale morphism of schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Since $\varphi$ is a map over $X$, $q\circ\varphi$ is the structure morphism of $Z$ over $X$, which is therefore etale.

source.place: Tag 025Y (definition-algebraic-space): representable etale maps tested on scheme base changes; an isomorphism of schemes is an open immersion, Morphisms Tag 02GP (lemma-open-immersion-etale).

proof_origin.place: Tags 03XU and 03XX, Section 0417 (schemehood); the final etaleness of Z over X is the item's chartwise hypothesis applied to the representing isomorphism.
